independent_source_findings.finding: A nonzero commit-hook result converts COMMIT into ROLLBACK. This is the SQLite documented API contract.

SQLite worker decrements tracked depth only after successful COMMIT/ROLLBACK. Transaction::commit returns early on error, then Drop queues a rollback. The subsequent rollback can fail because SQLite already rolled back; Ping acknowledges prior queue work without repairing tracked depth.
Return-to-pool and default checkout ping complete before before_acquire; Ok(false) closes this handle. is_in_transaction is exactly tracked depth != 0, not a new SQLite authority decision.

Frozen B vendor worker and transaction.rs are byte-identical to the verified published sqlite package. Guarded-only has no reuse hook; coordinated has an unconditional successful return after the owner callback. Both expose the same stale-depth risk.

The four frozen Memory interlock controls still prove physical COMMIT veto. Their explicit waiting/read-transaction probes issue BEGIN/COMMIT as raw SQL, bypassing SQLx Transaction depth bookkeeping; they do not exhaust this new Transaction API reuse path. No prior PASS is relabeled as FAIL.
